intro: Dutch elm disease emptied the village squares of Alicante province of their elms, and in Millena, a village of around two hundred people in El Comtat, one is still standing. The field elm in front of the Church of Sant Josep is locally called the thousand-year elm, and is more likely two to three centuries old. Its trunk is 5.30 metres round, its heavy limbs propped on pillars after a snowfall broke one. The village signposts it at the entrance to town. Free, in the open church square.
meta_description: The Olmo centenario de Millena, a field elm 5.30 metres round, survives in the church square of a small Alicante village. Free, in the open square.
question_meta: The Olmo centenario de Millena is a field elm of roughly 200 to 300 years in the church square of Millena, Alicante. Its story and how to find it.
question_answer: The Olmo centenario de Millena, locally the Om mil·lenari, is a field elm in the Plaza de la Iglesia in front of the Church of Sant Josep in Millena, a small village in the El Comtat district of Alicante province. Published estimates put it at about 300 years, and possibly nearer 200. Its trunk is 5.30 metres round, and it is free to see in the open square.
question_context: Dutch elm disease killed most of the old village elms of this part of Spain, and two independent accounts describe Millena's as the last healthy one still standing in a plaza in the province. The local name, the thousand-year elm, overstates it considerably. Published estimates say about three hundred years, and one travel writer who visited suggests it may be younger still: elms were planted in Spanish town squares to mark the Cádiz Constitution of 1812, and he wonders whether this is one of them. That is his theory rather than a record, so the honest range is somewhere between two and three centuries. The measurements are firmer. The trunk is 5.30 metres round, the tree about ten metres tall with a crown up to eleven metres across. A limb broke under snow, pillars were put in to hold up the rest, and a later snowfall damaged one of the pillars. The elm is not on the Valencian catalogue of monumental trees, but it is protected under the region's 2006 law on monumental trees. The most recent account we found dates from 2016, so a current report from a visitor would be welcome.

faq.q: Is the elm really a thousand years old?
faq.a: No. The local name means the thousand-year elm, but published estimates put it at about 300 years, and one visitor's theory would make it nearer 200.

Yes. It stands in the open church square in the centre of Millena, and the village signposts it at the entrance to town.
Millena is in inland Alicante province, between Gorga and Cocentaina, and no public transport reaches it. Drive from Cocentaina or Alcoi; it is roughly 65 kilometres from Alicante city.

trees.story:
Dutch elm disease killed the village elms of Alicante province one square at a time, and by two independent accounts this is the last healthy one still standing in a plaza. It grows in front of the Church of Sant Josep in Millena, a village of around two hundred people in El Comtat, and the village signposts it at the entrance to town.

Locally it is the Om mil·lenari, the thousand-year elm. It is not that old. The published estimates say about three hundred years, and one travel writer who visited suggests it may be younger still: elms were planted in Spanish town squares to mark the Cádiz Constitution of 1812, and he wonders whether this is one of them. That is his theory rather than a record, so hold both ideas loosely, somewhere between two and three centuries.

The measurements are firmer. The trunk is 5.30 metres round, the tree about ten metres tall with a crown up to eleven metres across, which is a great deal of wood for a field elm. Some of it has proved too heavy. A limb broke under snow, pillars were added to hold up the rest, and a later snowfall damaged one of the pillars.

It is not on the Valencian catalogue of monumental trees, but it is protected under the region's 2006 law on monumental trees. The most recent account we found is from 2016. If you have been since, tell us how it looks.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the support pillars propping up its heavy limbs and a trunk 5.30 metres round. It stands in the church square in front of the Church of Sant Josep, in the centre of Millena.
